name: metr_point_v0_head202_sharp4
rationale: The final MLP has an unusually large positive composed coefficient at neuron 202 (0.6184), but its median-selected activations are almost always dormant. Its negative GELU tail exceeds magnitude 0.01 at 215 calibration entries across 35 windows, where the median normalized residual is -0.080 and the mean -0.063. That tail therefore adds a downward contribution in an already underestimated subset. Sharpen this one gate by scaling its incoming row and bias by 2 and dividing its effective outgoing coefficient by 2: the contribution becomes c*GELU(2*x)/2. This suppresses the negative tail while preserving the zero threshold and positive linear asymptote, unlike deleting the feature. All other effective head coefficients remain fixed. Confirm on disjoint windows before interpreting this association as a useful repair. The factor-2 trial reduced calibration MSE by 0.0402% and MAE by 0.00673%, with uncertain MAE significance. Increase the same analytic gate sharpness to 4 to test further suppression of that tail; the positive linear asymptote remains unchanged.
